identity.title: Generator Matching: Generative modeling with arbitrary Markov processes

problem.claim: Develop a modality-agnostic generative-modeling framework based on arbitrary Markov processes.

contributions.claim: Introduces Generator Matching, which learns a marginal generator from conditional generators for individual data points.
Unifies diffusion models, flow matching, and discrete diffusion models while extending the design space to processes such as jump processes.
Provides a rigorous construction for superpositions of Markov generative models and multimodal models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Generator Matching by applying generator-based modeling to arbitrary Markov processes and enabling jump-process and rigorous superposition constructions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical validation on image and multimodal generation.
The authors report that superposition with a jump process improves performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generator Matching uses infinitesimal Markov-process generators for generative modeling, learning a marginal generator from conditional ones.
The framework is presented as encompassing several diffusion- and flow-based methods.
It extends the approach to previously unexplored Markov processes, including jump processes.
It supports rigorous superpositions and multimodal models, with reported image and multimodal experiments including a jump-process performance improvement.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a common generator-based formulation to existing methods, then uses that formulation to motivate new process choices and superpositions.

lessons.interpretation: A shared formal object can make unification and principled extensions part of the same contribution narrative.
lessons.application: When proposing a generative framework, define the common mathematical object, map established methods into it, and show which new design choices it makes expressible.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed method lacks a meaningful common formal representation or when method mapping would obscure important differences.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, metrics, baselines, magnitude of the reported improvement, or conditions under which jump-process superposition helps.
The abstract does not state an explicit limitation in prior approaches or establish priority beyond the authors' stated distinctions.
